title: NSPM-8: Winning the 6G Race — Phase 65 Discovery technologies review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Discovery technologies reporting pack. NSPM-8 frames U.S. leadership in 6G communications as a national-security and economic priority. The memorandum connects next-generation networks with AI, robotics, spectrum, resilient communications, standards, supply chains, and grid or industrial operations.
key_findings: 6G is treated as foundational infrastructure for economic and national-security systems.
Standards, spectrum, research, security, and trusted supply chains are central implementation fields.
Future networks are linked to AI, autonomy, robotics, and critical operations.
why_it_matters: Which records show a discovery instrument, dataset, testbed, or program becoming an inspectable research capability without treating availability as downstream use? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It identifies communications infrastructure and standards as dependencies for multiple frontier capabilities rather than as a standalone telecom issue.
ftfn_relevance: Supports tracking communications, compute, spectrum, standards, and equipment supply chains together.
Creates future watch questions for R&D programs, standards milestones, spectrum actions, and trusted equipment.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
6G remains an emerging standards and research field rather than a deployed national network.
The memorandum does not establish performance, cost, coverage, equipment availability, or adoption.
